item.title: Beaches
item.description:
Honestly, you can’t go wrong with beaches on Lanta — the west coast has many beaches. What follows is a guide to how they differ so you can pick the right one for the day.

Khlong Dao Beach #

Khlong Dao Beach - The northernmost of the main beaches, closest to Saladan. A long, wide stretch of gently shelving sand that’s great for swimming and families, with plenty of restaurants, bars and resorts along the back. Recommended bar: Majestic bar

Long Beach (Phra Ae) #

Long Beach - Just south of Khlong Dao and, as the name suggests, very long. A popular base with lots of accommodation, beach bars and sunset spots, but still spacious enough to find a quiet stretch. Lym’s Bar is where most nomads go for sunset drinks.

Nui Bay #

Nui Bay - A small, beautiful cove reached by some steep steps. There are no real facilities here — sometimes there are monkeys, and sometimes someone selling drinks, but that’s about it. Come for the scenery and seclusion rather than amenities, keep an eye on your belongings around the monkeys, and bring what you need with you.

Beautiful Beach & Secret Beach #

Beautiful Beach - A gorgeous cove further south. Since 2026 there is a parking fee, and a gate that is closed at night, so plan around that if you’re heading out for sunset.

Secret Beach - Tucked in right next to Beautiful Beach. To reach it you park at Beautiful Beach and walk over — there’s no separate access — so the same parking fee and night gate apply. No facilities and no bars.

item.title: Coworking
item.description:
The island has fiber internet along the west coast from Saladan down to Klong Nin. Cafes average around 180 Mbps, and the dedicated coworking spaces hit 1 Gbps. You won’t have connectivity problems here.

Coworking spaces #

KoHub #

KoHub is the biggest coworking space on the island. It’s off the main road near Long Beach, about 10 minutes walk from the sand, with a jungle garden out back. The internet is fast (1 Gbps fiber), there’s good coffee and food on site, and the community is the main draw. People come back year after year.

item.title: Visa
item.description:
93 countries get 60 days visa-free. That’s enough for most visitors. You can extend by 30 days at immigration if you want to stay longer, or apply for a tourist visa (60 days) before your trip.

⚠️ Heads up: Thailand has approved cutting visa-free stays from 60 to 30 days for most nationalities (and fewer eligible countries). It’s not in effect yet as of mid-2026, but it could take effect at short notice — always check the current rule before you book.

item.title: Getting to Koh Lanta
item.description:
Most people fly into Krabi and take a road transfer. From Bangkok, count on 5-6 hours door to door: the flight itself is short, but the transfer and ferry crossing eat up the rest.

Fly to Krabi, then drive #

Krabi Airport is the closest airport. Direct flights from Bangkok take about 1.5 hours. Thai Airways and Bangkok Airways fly from Suvarnabhumi (BKK). Budget airlines like AirAsia, Nok Air, and Thai Lion Air fly from Don Mueang (DMK).

item.title: Trips & Activities
item.description:
Cooking Classes #

Time for Lime #

The original Thai cooking school on Koh Lanta, open since 2002. Located on Klong Dao Beach in an open-air beachfront setting with a pool. Classes run ~5.5 hours — you make curry paste, 2 starters, and 2 main courses, then eat what you cooked. A cocktail class is included in some packages. Recipes are sent home with you.

A portion of all profits goes to Lanta Animal Welfare, which rescues and treats stray animals on the island.

item.title: Accommodation
item.description:
Most nomads stay around Long Beach (Phra Ae) since it’s close to KoHub. Prices vary a lot by season. High season (Dec-Feb) books up fast and costs roughly double what you’d pay in shoulder months (Nov, Mar-Apr). If you’re coming in peak season, book ahead. Outside of that, you can often just show up and walk around.

Some places are cheaper when you message them directly on WhatsApp or Facebook. Monthly rates are almost always negotiable in person.

item.title: Sports
item.description:
Gyms #

WM Fitness - Long Beach area. Modern gym with good selection of cardio equipment, resistance machines, and free weights. Also has a rig area with battle ropes, sandbags, kettlebells. Connected to William Muay Thai Stadium. Air conditioned. Day pass 200 THB. See Facebook for full pricing information.

Luke’s Gym - European style gym in Klong Khong, surrounded by jungle. Dumbbells up to 50kg, many machines. Very clean with separate changing rooms and showers. Towels provided. Air conditioned. Protein shakes available (vegetarian/vegan options, 120 THB). Day pass 200 THB, see lukesgym.com for more pricing information. You need a scooter to get there.

item.title: Is there Grab on Koh Lanta?
item.description:
No. Grab doesn’t work on Koh Lanta, and neither does Bolt or any other ride-hailing app. The island is too small and too far from the mainland for any of them to operate here.

If you’re coming from Bangkok, Chiang Mai, or even Krabi town, you’re used to opening an app and having a car show up. That won’t happen here. Put the phone away and read on.

How people actually get around #

Most people rent a scooter. The island is about 30km from north to south, so even the longest ride takes maybe 40 minutes. Rentals run 250-300 THB per day, less if you’re renting by the month. There are rental shops everywhere, especially around Saladan.

item.title: Transportation
item.description:
There’s no public transport on Koh Lanta. Most people rent a scooter and that’s pretty much all you need. The island is about 30km from north to south, so even the longest trip only takes around 40 minutes.

Ride-hailing isn’t an option either: there’s no Grab on Koh Lanta, and no Bolt or anything similar. Scooters and call-ahead taxis are what everyone uses.

item.title: Money
item.description:
Cash is king on Koh Lanta. Most local restaurants, massage shops, markets and small businesses only accept cash. Bigger restaurants, hotels and convenience stores like 7-Eleven take Visa and Mastercard, but don’t count on it everywhere. Always have cash on hand.

Photo by Q L on Pexels (free to use)

ATMs #

ATMs are scattered across the island, mostly at 7-Elevens and bank branches. You’ll find them in Saladan, Klong Dao, Long Beach and Klong Nin. There are two banks in Saladan (SCB and TTB), and a Kasikorn ATM near Southern Lanta Resort at Klong Dao Beach.
